Subject: ACME: feature parity follow-up — function calling, structured outputs & streaming

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through ACME's integration goals and the evaluation criteria. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap (5m):
- Primary use case: real-time product assistant in the ACME dashboard (low latency, streaming responses)
- Must-haves: deterministic structured outputs (JSON schema), tool/function calling for lookups/actions, streaming for progressive render, and a predictable cost model for 100k monthly active users
- Primary concerns you raised: latency under 200ms p50 for short responses, API parity with current hyperscaler features (function call patterns, streaming chunking), and SOC2 evidence for procurement review

Suggested next tests (we can provide infra + scripts):
1) Function calling parity: end-to-end test invoking a mock inventory lookup and verifying the call/response pattern and rollback semantics.
2) Structured outputs: validate strict JSON schema adherence across edge cases (nested lists, optional fields).
3) Streaming behavior: compare streaming chunk latency and order guarantees versus your current provider.
4) Perf baseline: 1k concurrent users simulating typical prompt sizes to capture p50/p95 latency and throughput.

I attached a proposed evaluation matrix (ACME-eval-matrix.xlsx) and a short recording of today's demo — recording link in my next email.

Proposed timeline: run the tests next week (start Mon 6/15), with a short sync after 72h of runs to review results. If that works, I'll loop in our infra team for a short walkthrough of the staging endpoints and share a temporary key.

Next actions for ACME: please confirm (a) the test window (we suggested 6/15–6/18), and (b) who on your side will own the test harness so we can share the script and the sample test cases.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Hey Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — that captures the call well. A few quick clarifications: 

- For function calling, we need the ability to return structured metadata along with the tool invocation (e.g., confidence scores + tool execution logs). Can Redwood include these in the payload?
- For streaming, how does Redwood handle partial structured outputs? If we stream JSON fragments, how do you guarantee the final merged object is schema-valid?
- Regarding SOC2 evidence, procurement asked if you can share the external-facing SOC2 report and a short note on retention/audit logs — would be great if your security contact could send that over.

We can commit to the 6/15 window. I'll own the test harness on our side — I'll loop in Tom (platform) if we need infra help.

Also, can you send the demo recording and a staging API key? We'll try to run the function-calling test first.

Best,

Thanks Alice — great to hear 6/15 works. Quick notes addressing your questions and next artifacts attached: 

1) Function calling payloads: yes — our function call response includes an optional metadata block (executed_by, exec_time_ms, confidence_score). We'll include logs in the response payload and can also stream tool logs as a separate channel if you'd like. Sample payload attached in the eval matrix.

2) Streaming + partial structured outputs: our runtime supports both chunked text streaming and a streaming-JSON mode. For the latter we emit well-formed JSON fragments followed by a finalization event; our client SDK merges fragments and validates the final object against the provided schema. We included a small JS snippet in the eval matrix that demonstrates merge/validation behavior. Edge cases we recommend testing: nested arrays with partial flushes, and interrupted streams where SDK must rehydrate from last checkpoint.

3) SOC2: our security team provided the external SOC2 report link — attaching pointer and the short retention/audit summary.

Artifacts attached/sent:
- ACME-eval-matrix.xlsx (detailed test cases + sample payloads)
- demo-recording-20260608.mp4 (recording of today's demo uploaded to Drive)
- redwood-staging-api-key.txt (one-time staging key + instructions)
- SOC2-report-link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-evals (permission granted to acme.com domain)

Suggested test runner checklist (we'll provide templates):
- Run function-calling test (10 calls/min for 30m) — verify invocation metadata and logs
- Run structured output validation suite (20 schema cases) — pass/fail per case with sample prompts
- Streaming comparison (compare first-byte latency and chunk arrival pattern vs your current provider)

I'll loop in David and Marcus to provision a short-lived staging endpoint and coordinate runs next week. Expect a separate email with the staging URL and the API key.

Thanks,
Marissa
